title: A fully faithful continuous cocontinuous bigger-site inclusion has a retraction
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor. Assume (a) $u$ is cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1); (b) $u$ is continuous [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3); (c) $u$ is fully faithful, meaning that every map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(uX,uY)$ is bijective; (d) fibre products exist in $\mathcal C$ and $u$ preserves them; and (e) $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ have final objects $e_{\mathcal C},e_{\mathcal D}$ and $u(e_{\mathcal C})\cong e_{\mathcal D}$. Write $R:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ for restriction, $(RG)(X)=G(uX)$, and $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for the sheafified presheaf left adjoint $L(F)=(u_pF)^\#$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3). Then $u$ defines a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ with $f_*=R$, $f^{-1}=L$, and a geometric morphism $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with $g^{-1}=R$. The adjunctions are $L\dashv R\dashv g_*$. The canonical unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}\to RL$ of $L\dashv R$ and the canonical counit $Rg_*\to\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}$ of $R\dashv g_*$ are isomorphisms. In particular $f\circ g$ is isomorphic to the identity geometric morphism and $L=f^{-1}$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tags 00XU (lemma-bigger-site), 00XT (lemma-back-and-forth), 00XR (lemma-when-shriek); 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism) supplies the morphism of sites

proof.text: First check finite limits. A terminal object and fibre products give binary products $X\times Y=X\times_{e_{\mathcal C}}Y$. The equalizer of $a,b:X\rightrightarrows Y$ is the pullback of $(a,b):X\to Y\times Y$ and the diagonal $Y\to Y\times Y$. Thus these constructions give finite limits in $\mathcal C$. Hypotheses (d) and (e), with the chosen isomorphism $u(e_{\mathcal C})\cong e_{\mathcal D}$, carry these very terminal objects, products and equalizers to their counterparts in $\mathcal D$, so $u$ preserves finite limits. Continuity means in particular that $u$ sends every covering family to a covering family [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).

source.place: Tag 00XU (lemma-bigger-site), hypotheses (d),(e), verifying the finite-limit hypotheses of Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism)

proof.text: Use the common-universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], taking the sheaf values in a containing universe. Apply the set-sheaf clause of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to the finite limits and image-covering condition just checked. It gives exactly the sheafified left Kan extension $L(F)=(u_pF)^\#$, its adjunction $L\dashv R$, and preservation of finite limits and all colimits by $L$. Hence $u$ defines a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), with $f_*=R$ and $f^{-1}=L$. The same adjunction is the geometric morphism on sheaf topoi in [def-trf-geometric-morphism].

source.place: Tags 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism), 00X1 (definition-morphism-sites), 00XC (lemma-morphism-sites-topoi), and 00XU (lemma-bigger-site), first paragraph of proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] using precisely hypotheses (a),(b). Its functor called $L$ there is our restriction $R$, and its functor called $R$ there is our $g_*$. It supplies the geometric morphism $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ with $g^{-1}=R$ and $R\dashv g_*$. For $F\in\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, sections of $g_*F$ over $V$ are the compatible families $(s_{A,\psi})$ for $\psi:uA\to V$. In this model the counit $\varepsilon_F:Rg_*F\to F$, evaluated at $X$, sends a family to $s_{X,\mathrm{id}_{uX}}$. Together with step 2 this is the adjoint triple $L\dashv R\dashv g_*$.

source.place: Tags 00XO (lemma-cocontinuous-morphism-topoi) and 00XR (lemma-when-shriek); Tag 00XT (lemma-back-and-forth), first paragraph of proof

proof.text: Compute the inverse of this counit explicitly. Fix $X\in\mathcal C$. By full faithfulness, every $\psi:uA\to uX$ is uniquely $u(a)$ for $a:A\to X$. Given $t\in F(X)$, put $s_{A,u(a)}=F(a)(t)$. These entries satisfy compatibility: for $b:B\to A$, $F(b)(F(a)(t))=F(a\circ b)(t)$. Conversely the compatibility equation for $a:A\to X$ and the identity of $uX$ gives $s_{A,u(a)}=F(a)(s_{X,\mathrm{id}_{uX}})$. Thus evaluation at the identity and this construction are inverse functions. For $h:X'\to X$ and $a:A\to X'$, restriction of this family has coordinate $F(h\circ a)(t)=F(a)(F(h)(t))$ at $u(a)$, which proves naturality in $X$. A morphism $F\to F'$ commutes with the construction by its naturality. Therefore these inverses give an inverse natural transformation to the canonical counit $\varepsilon:Rg_*\to\operatorname{id}$. Only the compatible-family and counit formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] are used here; no density hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 00XT (lemma-back-and-forth), first paragraph: fully faithful pointwise evaluation of the right adjoint

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-adjoint-triple-unit-counit] to the actual adjunctions $L\dashv R\dashv g_*$ of steps 2 and 3. Since their second counit is the isomorphism of step 4, their first unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to RL$ is an isomorphism. This is the canonical unit for the sheafified $L=(u_p\,)^\#$, since it is the unit of that very first adjunction. Thus both canonical back-and-forth maps required in the statement have now been proved invertible.

source.place: Tag 00XT (lemma-back-and-forth), two canonical isomorphisms; unit deduced formally from the proved counit by Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Triple.lean:66-75

proof.text: By the composition convention of [def-trf-geometric-morphism], $(f\circ g)_*=f_*g_*=Rg_*$. The counit isomorphism $Rg_*\cong\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}$ from step 4 is therefore a natural isomorphism of direct-image functors from $f\circ g$ to the identity. The same definition identifies such an isomorphism with an invertible $2$-morphism (and with its inverse-image mate). Consequently $f\circ g$ is isomorphic to the identity geometric morphism.

source.place: Tag 00XU (lemma-bigger-site), first paragraph of proof: identity composite

proof.text: Finally let $F,G\in\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. For $b:LF\to LG$, its adjunct is $R(b)\circ\eta_F:F\to RLG$. Define $a=\eta_G^{-1}\circ R(b)\circ\eta_F:F\to G$. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $R(L(a))\circ\eta_F=\eta_G\circ a=R(b)\circ\eta_F$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $L(a)=b$. Conversely if $b=L(a)$, the same naturality equation makes the displayed formula recover $a$. Thus the actual map $a\mapsto L(a)$ on each Hom set has this explicit inverse. Hence $L=f^{-1}$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 00XU (lemma-bigger-site), last paragraph of proof: the adjunction Hom-set bijection and the invertible unit
